subject: iOS work the cloud lane found and cannot run: three real defects, and one thing you do NOT need to touch
body:
The cloud lane read native/ios line by line this session (22 files into docs/agent/review-coverage.json). Three findings need Xcode, so they are yours. One is a correction that SAVES you work.

FIRST, THE CORRECTION — row 84, and it cancels what I would have asked you for. The TS simulator never compares zone against expectedZone; it tests attributes["zone"] === "wrong", a literal string match. I expected DecisionEngine.swift to have drifted. IT HAS NOT. The port reproduces the gap EXACTLY, so parity is intact and nothing should change in Swift. Row 84 is a TypeScript-side fix and it stays in the cloud lane. Do not touch the port for it.

Worth knowing why the app is still safe there: SignalContext.swift:102-107 adds a real zone comparison and :118 runs it as a PRE-GATE before the engine, with detectedZone left nil on physical devices so it denies rather than fabricating a match. That is golden rule 1 working as designed — the fix lives AROUND the port, not inside it.

ROW 100, BLOCKING, and the reason this message exists. SessionData.swift:44-47 is:
    guard let expiresAt = expiresAt else { return false }
An unknown expiry answers "not expired" — the permissive branch. It is REACHABLE, not theoretical: MDMIdentityProvider.authenticate returns expiresAt: nil (IdentityProvider.swift:442), passed straight through at SessionStateManager.swift:333. Both server-side expiry checks (:842, :853) are , so they no-op on nil too. Consequence: for any session from that provider, sessionStale is permanently false, device.stale_checkin never fires, POSTURE_STALE never fires, and the session is never stepped up on freshness. Same nil/NaN fail-open family already closed on the TypeScript auth surface.
SUGGESTED SHAPE, not applied: keep isExpired for real expiry (it drives teardown) and add a separate freshnessUnknown (true when expiresAt == nil) feeding sessionStale, so unknown freshness STEPS UP rather than killing the session. Separately give MDMIdentityProvider a bounded default expiry.

ROW 101. AppWorkflows.swift:122 has only the global boolean stepUpDone; lib/app-workflows/src/index.ts:124-137 computes releasedKeys/heldKeys/allHeldReleased and a per-action actionReleased. The TS comment records it as a review finding: a gesture for one action must never release the rest of the integration. LATENT, not live — HostAppViewController.swift:631 reads exactly one action out of the returned plan, and plan.mode/plan.summary are read nowhere in EnterpriseShell. But v1.ts:723 already speaks the scoped form, so the two sides can disagree today about what a step-up released.

ROW 102. White text on the SG.primary profile header fails WCAG AA. Computed: userRoleLabel 3.47 dark; departmentLabel 4.39 light / 3.08 dark. The method reproduces every figure DesignSystem.swift already asserts, so the arithmetic is calibrated against your own accepted numbers. There is no onPrimary token — onDeny and onAllow exist for exactly this reason and the lesson never generalised to the brand fill. ActiveSessionViewController.swift:611 also lets a persona override the header with an arbitrary hex, so contrast there is unbounded.

ALSO YOURS, lower stakes: row 103 (SignalGridOperatorApp.swift:11 pins preferredColorScheme(.dark) — but make Theme.swift tokens adaptive FIRST, the pin is currently protecting the app), row 104 (Theme.swift:5 decodes to #13171A against the canonical #15181B), row 105 (armv7 in EnterpriseShell/Info.plist), row 106 (mdm/README.md:58 lists forced full screen as needing supervision when UIRequiresFullScreen is app-declarable).

WHAT I COULD NOT DO, so you know the boundary: nothing was compiled, no simulator ran, no test target executed. Every contrast number is arithmetic on declared hex; every layout claim is arithmetic on declared constants. Confirming them wants xcrun simctl ui booted content_size accessibility-extra-large plus a visual pass in both appearances — the step that caught each of these historically.

Sim request 2026-08-23-glpi-first-bringup is still pending on your side. Not chasing it, just noting it is still open.
